subject: factor scores using covariates on a group data

messages.author: 833e408d3daa461d
messages.subject: factor scores using covariates on a group data
parts:
Hi Phil, 

I have a dataframe with two items. I am giving a short version of my data to get an idea. 

dat = data.frame(Item1 = c(1,1,2,3,0,1,3,5), Item2 = c(1,2,4,1,2,3,1,4)) 

The first 4 response belongs to time = 1 week, the second 4 at time = 3week. 

I want to build a mirt model with the latent regression term as 

covdata = data.frame(group = rep(1,4), rep(3,4))

model1 <- 'F1 = 1,
          F2 = 2'

model1 = mirt.model(model1)

mod1 = mirt(dat, model = model1, covdata = covdata, formula = ~group)

which worked perfectly fine. 

But when I am extracting the latent scores of an outside response sheet as 

fscores(mod1, response.pattern = c(1,2))

It gives an error message as 

Error in rep(TRUE, nrow(tabdata)) : invalid 'times' argument

I am not sure why I am getting this error. I tried looking for help, but cannot get around any help on this. Please help me identify my error, or how can I obtain factor scores for an external response sheet from my IRT model already developed. 

Thanks

Souvik

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: factor scores using covariates on a group data
parts:
Two things here: 1) the model is not identified, you need at least 3 items per latent trait (preferably more), and 2) the response.pattern input will not work with latent regression effects because there is not enough information (what are the associated IV terms for this given response pattern?). 

If you have an IRT model which is already developed, parameters and all, then you'll probably want to setup your model without estimation. There are several ways to do this in the package, so just look through the manual and forum to find an answer (I've posted this on cross-validated as well). Cheers.

Phil

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: factor scores using covariates on a group data
parts: Hi Souvik,
On Fri, Aug 12, 2016 at 2:34 PM, Souvik Bhattacharya <souvi...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Phil,
1) the model is not identified, you need at least 3 items per latent trait (preferably more),
I want to find a relationship between Item 1 and Item 2. That is why i defined individual latent trait for each item .

Yes, but simply defining them this way does not make the model identifiable. More constraints are required (e.g., the slopes would have to be set to 1 and not estimated). And even then, including latent regression effects doesn't seem worthwhile because the latent trait will have a fixed amount of variability.

2) the response.pattern input will not work with latent regression effects because there is not enough information (what are the associated IV terms for this given response pattern?)

I wish to obtain the latent score at time = 1 week (say). Is there a way to enter that information in the response pattern for obtaining the latent score.

Yes, but you are still missing the covdata terms for this response pattern. What group is the pattern c(1,2) associated with? How would fscores() know this information?

That being said, isn't this just a simple chi-squared test of association (or if you care about group information, a log-linear test)? If all you have is two items then IRT isn't really required here.

messages.subject: Re: factor scores using covariates on a group data
parts:
Thanks Phil. I see I was not passing the group information and definitely it makes perfect sense that the program wont know about the group information .  Thanks for your suggestion. 

I modified my fscores to 

fscores(mod1, response.pattern = c(1,2), covdata = data.frame(group = 1)) and it worked perfectly fine. 

Thanks
Souvik
